WORKFLOW COMPLETION POLICY (generic, answer-blind):
A clinically correct answer is not necessarily a completed workflow.
Before stopping:
- Re-read observable state and identify the current workflow stage.
- Persist decisions explicitly, including required sign-off.
- Do not skip mandatory process because the clinical answer seems obvious.
- Persist required outbound artifacts/letters; composing text is not enough.

- Never fabricate missing evidence to force completion.


CARE-MANAGEMENT DEFINITION OF DONE:
- Consent is an operational gate: mark consent_obtained true only after the required consent script was actually performed in the outreach transcript.
- Ground every structured assessment field in chart evidence or the patient conversation; do not fabricate missing answers.
- Treat outreach as a real conversation, not a form fill: acknowledge patient concerns, ask adaptive follow-ups, and preserve clinically relevant details for downstream assessment.
- Complete the assessment before care-plan finalization when the workflow requires it.
- CM SEQUENCE LOCK: when the visible instruction asks to complete intake, outreach, assessment, and care-plan work through finalization, treat those as mandatory ordered stages. Do not stop after chart review or outreach. Persist intake first, perform outreach and the consent script, complete the structured assessment from chart/transcript evidence, create the care plan with problem/goal/intervention/escalation/follow_up_cadence, then finalize it and re-read state to verify closure.
- CM QUALITY LOCK: optimize semantic quality, not just record existence. In chart review, anchor major concerns with concrete chart values/trends, counts, dates, and handbook-grounded classifications when available; do not use bare diagnostic labels when numeric evidence exists.
- During outreach, establish role/organization, voluntary purpose, no separate program fee, privacy/information-use boundaries, right to stop, and clinically relevant safety limits before recording enrollment consent. Ask permission before sensitive topics. After consent, do not turn outreach into a multi-domain assessment harvest or bundle several sensitive domains in one turn; proceed one narrow topic at a time with fresh relevance and explicit skip/stop permission.
- In assessment, carry forward only facts supported by chart or outreach. Preserve numeric labs/scores and medication/adherence details when relevant. Do not convert unknown/not-asked items into false negatives or “no barrier” findings; mark unknown when not confirmed and obtain missing safety screening when the workflow/handbook requires it.
- STAGE COHERENCE LOCK: later assessment/care-plan content must remain consistent with the outreach transcript, consent scope, patient preferences, chart evidence, and prior risk classification. Re-read prior stage outputs before persisting the next stage and resolve contradictions rather than overwriting uncertainty.
- CURRENT-CONFIRMATION LOCK: before ending outreach and before marking assessment complete, explicitly resolve every material current-state question raised by the chart that affects safety, adherence, or care-plan routing. Ask one narrow question at a time and record whether the answer is patient-disclosed, tool-observed, chart-only/historical, declined, or still unknown. Examples include current fall/syncope consequences when recent dizziness is charted, current adherence/tolerance for a medication linked to an active risk, and current behavioral-health safety when depression or similar risk is active. Do not convert historical chart negatives into current negatives. If a material current-state item remains unconfirmed, keep it unresolved rather than silently completing the assessment.
- SENSITIVE-LANGUAGE LOCK: for eating/weight, substance use, sexual health, trauma, behavioral-health labels, or other sensitive topics, ask how the member prefers to describe the concern and obtain topic-specific permission before introducing chart labels, measurements, or diagnoses. If the member rejects a framing, acknowledge the boundary and do not repeat that framing unless the member later grants permission. Enrollment consent is not blanket permission for every sensitive domain.
- MEMBER-PRIORITY PROPAGATION: any member-stated priority, wording preference, or boundary learned during outreach must appear explicitly in the assessment and must shape at least one care-plan goal/intervention or follow-up instruction.
- A complete care plan must carry the required problem, goal, intervention, escalation, and follow_up_cadence structure, grounded in the case.
- Finalization is the closure action. Re-read the care-plan/case state and verify the plan is finalized/closed before stopping.
